title: Frost on the Pond
checkpoint: Reception Summer 2, week 3 — Phase 4: Three consonants together: three consonant sounds together (no new sounds)
note_for_grown_ups: More Phase 4 practice with consonant blends at the start of words: frost, slip, spin. Say the two sounds close together but keep them separate.

pages.text: It was crisp. Frost was on the pond.
pages.illustration: Wide winter morning: the pond frozen and white, reeds stiff with frost, everything blue and silver. Beautiful and very cold.

pages.text: Ned had to slip and slam.
pages.illustration: Ned stepping onto the ice with one foot, other foot still on the bank, an expression of doubt. The instant before it goes wrong.

pages.text: Ned went flat on the frost!
pages.illustration: Ned flat on his front on the ice, legs splayed in all four directions, beak on the frost. Seen from directly above. Extremely funny.
Ned sliding helplessly across the whole width of the page still lying flat, with a look of resignation. Long horizontal composition.

pages.text: Moss ran out of the den.
pages.illustration: Moss bursting out of his leaf pile den at the bank, spikes bristling, at full hedgehog speed (which is not fast).
Moss at the ice edge with one paw out, shouting; Ned still on his back some distance away, waving one foot. Comic distance between them.
Ned spinning on the ice like a top, wings out, blurred, delighted. Circular motion lines and a happy face in the middle.
Both of them on the ice now, Moss sliding on his tummy, Ned spinning, ice shavings flying. Full of joy and movement.

pages.text: Ned and Moss went back in.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the two of them heading back into the leaf den at dusk, frost on their backs, warm dark hole ahead of them.
